title: Best Children's Online Safety Tools Compared
metaDescription: Qustodio, Norton Family and Apple Screen Time compared on web filtering, time limits, location, social media monitoring and device support.
intro: Protecting your children online takes the right tools. This page compares three parental control options, Qustodio, Norton Family and Apple Screen Time, on content filtering, time limits, location, social media monitoring and device support, using the makers' published features and pricing.

products.name: Qustodio
products.tagline: Parental control app with web filtering, time limits and location tracking
products.pricing: Free plan (1 device); paid Basic and Complete plans billed yearly, with prices that vary by country
pros: Excellent content filtering across all devices
Detailed activity reports and location tracking
Message alerts for WhatsApp, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and X (most on Android only)
cons: Free plan covers one device, with limited features
Most social media message alerts work only on Android

products.name: Norton Family
products.tagline: Norton's parental control app, sold on its own or with Norton 360
products.pricing: $49.99/year on its own; included with Norton 360 Deluxe and higher plans
pros: Alerts when a child arrives at or leaves a saved place
cons: No macOS or Chromebook support, and fewer controls on iPhone than on Android
Interface can be overwhelming for new users

products.name: Apple Screen Time
products.tagline: Apple's built-in parental controls for iPhone, iPad and Mac
products.pricing: Free, built into iPhone, iPad and Mac

features.name: Content Filtering
features.description: Blocks inappropriate websites and content based on categories and age settings

qustodio.note: Category-based web filtering with custom rules

screen-time-ios.note: Basic content restrictions, limited web filtering

features.name: Screen Time Management
features.description: Controls and monitors how much time children spend on devices and apps

qustodio.note: Detailed time limits per app and device

norton-family.note: Time limits and schedules; limits can't be enforced on iPhone

screen-time-ios.note: Built-in iOS controls with family sharing

features.name: Location Tracking
features.description: Monitors child's physical location for safety and peace of mind

norton-family.note: Location tracking with alerts for saved places

screen-time-ios.note: Find My integration with location sharing

features.name: Social Media Monitoring
features.description: Tracks activity and interactions on social platforms for safety risks

qustodio.note: AI alerts on WhatsApp, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and X messages; most are Android-only

norton-family.note: No social media or message monitoring

screen-time-ios.note: App limits, and Communication Safety nudity warnings in Apple's apps; no social media monitoring

features.name: Multi-Device Support
features.description: Works across different operating systems and device types

qustodio.note: Windows, Mac, Android, iOS, Chromebook and Kindle

norton-family.note: Windows, Android and iOS; no Mac or Chromebook

verdict.summary: Qustodio scores highest on this table: strong web filtering, time limits, location and the widest device support, though most of its message alerts work only on Android. Norton Family comes second, with strong web filtering and location tracking for $49.99 a year on its own, but it has no social media monitoring and no Mac or Chromebook support. Apple Screen Time is free and built in, with good time limits, but it only works on Apple devices and its web filtering is basic.

bestFor.useCase: Families with a mix of devices
bestFor.reason: Highest score here, and it runs on Windows, Mac, Android, iOS, Chromebook and Kindle
Built into iPhone, iPad and Mac at no extra cost, with downtime schedules and app limits
Included with Norton 360 Deluxe and higher plans, and also sold on its own

pro_tips: Start with open conversations about online safety before implementing any monitoring tools - transparency builds trust and cooperation.
Use age-appropriate settings and gradually increase freedom as children demonstrate responsible online behavior and digital literacy.
Regularly review and update content filters as children grow, ensuring restrictions remain relevant and not overly restrictive for their maturity level.
Consider combining tools - for example, Screen Time on Apple devices with a cross-platform app such as Qustodio if your family also uses Android or Windows.
Set up family media agreements that clearly outline expectations, consequences, and the reasoning behind safety measures you've implemented.

faqs.question: What age should I start using parental control tools?
faqs.answer: Start as soon as your child begins using internet-connected devices, typically around age 5-7. Adjust settings and gradually reduce restrictions as they demonstrate responsible behavior and digital maturity.

faqs.question: Do parental control tools slow down internet speed?
faqs.answer: It depends on the tool and the device. Apps that filter on the child's device run in the background there, while filters on a router or a DNS service work on the network instead. If a device slows down after you install one, check the app's settings or try a network-level filter.

faqs.question: How do I protect my child's privacy while keeping them safe?
faqs.answer: Choose tools with clear data practices and check what each one records about your child. Prefer filtering and time limits over recording everything, explain what is monitored and why, and move from monitoring toward agreed rules as your child gets older.

faqs.question: Can children bypass parental control software?
faqs.answer: Tech-savvy children may find workarounds, but modern tools are increasingly difficult to bypass. The key is combining technology with education and open communication about online safety.

faqs.question: What's the difference between free and paid parental control tools?
faqs.answer: Free versions typically offer basic filtering and time limits, while paid versions include advanced features like social media monitoring, location tracking, detailed reports, and multi-device support.

faqs.question: Do I need parental controls if my child only uses educational apps?
faqs.answer: Yes, even educational apps can contain links to external websites, chat features, or ads that lead to inappropriate content. Basic protection is recommended regardless of intended use.
